_meta.description: 21 synthetic Indian documents held out as a test set: two ID cards, an Aadhaar card, and eighteen everyday forms, bills, invoices, letters, receipts and labels. 118 PII items, 14 of them sensitive-tier.
_meta.source: OpenAI image generation, prompted by the repository owner — 11 pages 2026-09-18, 10 more added 2026-09-19
_meta.licence: Fully synthetic — every name, number, address and face is fabricated; no real person and no real document. OpenAI assigns output rights to the user; purely AI-generated output generally cannot be copyrighted for want of human authorship, so nothing restricts redistribution. The repository's MIT licence covers the human-directed selection, curation and annotation. Same status as datasets/documents/, which is likewise entirely AI-generated (01-10 by a Claude-written renderer, 11-20 by an OpenAI image model). See SOURCES.md.
_meta.annotation: text (legibility scoring); no boxes — see note_no_boxes
_meta.held_out_rule: THIS CORPUS MAY NEVER BE USED TO TUNE ANY OCR SYSTEM. Not backend selection, not PSM, not upscale factors, not preprocessing variants, not thresholds. Scoring it once with an already-chosen configuration is its purpose and is allowed; sweeping configurations over it and keeping the winner is forbidden. Set by the repository owner, 2026-09-18, as an absolute and permanent condition of the corpus being here. redactor.datasets.refuse_if_tuning() enforces it and test_holdout_guard.py pins it.
_meta.evidence_status: NOT independent evidence. The repository owner generated these images, so they carry the same standing as datasets/documents/: a ceiling on familiar material. Held-out discipline stops the corpus being tuned against, which is worth real money; it does not make it third-party data. Independent evidence still comes from datasets/cheques/, IndiaPII-Bench and maskara.
_meta.note_no_boxes: No box coordinates. The only way to produce them for these images is a vision pass, and per-region coverage from vision boxes was built, measured and removed here because those boxes sit about a text row off. Text-only, like datasets/documents/.
_meta.note_resolution: Images 03-11 are roughly 471x363, so character heights are small and the upscale-by-character-height path carries most of the load. A low score on those pages may be measuring resolution rather than detection. Images 01 and 02 are full resolution (1536x1024 and 1427x1102).
_meta.note_watermarks: Every page except 01 carries a printed 'SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT' watermark, which is real ink on the page and will be OCR'd as text.
_meta.note_filenames: Filenames carry an 'h' prefix so they cannot collide with another corpus's. They did: holdout's 01_aadhaar_card.png matched documents' exactly, and a score run without REDACTOR_CORPUS=holdout silently graded that one page against the wrong ground truth and reported '4 redacted, 1 leaked' as if it were a whole-corpus result. A prefix turns that silent half-success into an obvious zero-match.
_meta.corpus_revision: 2026-09-19: grew from 11 images / 71 items to 21 / 118. Scores before and after that change are NOT comparable — the denominator moved, not the pipeline. The two earlier holdout entries in benchmarks/history.jsonl (78.9% and 77.5%, both on 11 images) belong to the smaller corpus. The report refuses to draw a delta across a change in image count.
_meta.note_visual: The 2026-09-19 additions were chosen partly to fix a measurement gap: QR ground truth went from 4 regions to 9, which is why the detector's QR precision and recall can now be read with something better than four true positives behind them.

pii.note: The only Devanagari value in any image corpus here. The label lexicon carries Devanagari terms that no image has exercised.

Verhoeff checksum FAILS (verified). IN_AADHAAR discards checksum failures rather than down-scoring them, so only the OCR-tolerant fallback can cover this. Second canary for that fallback, alongside documents/04_hospital_admission_report.png.

h01_aadhaar_card.png.notes: Photorealistic Aadhaar card on a wooden surface. Gender (महिला / Female) is not annotated, matching documents/. NOTE: this is the one image here that carries NO 'synthetic test document' watermark, so SOURCES.md's caveat about reproducing official Indian layouts applies most strongly to it. Every value on it is fabricated.

pii.text: 12, Green Park Avenue, Indiranagar, Bengaluru - 560038, Karnataka, India

pii.note: Appears twice: in the box top-right and again as the barcode's printed value. Both must be covered. No published spec, so no recognizer — a labels.py case.

h02_community_services_id_card.png.notes: The richest page in the corpus: face, barcode, QR, contact details and two sensitive-tier medical fields on one sheet. 'Medical Conditions: None' is deliberately NOT annotated — the value is the word 'None', so there is nothing to conceal and a legibility verdict on it would be meaningless. Registration Date and Valid Till are document dates, not personal ones, and are not annotated either.

pii.note: The leading glyph is the LETTER S, not a 5 — verified at 8x. A quirk of the generator's font, recorded verbatim because ground truth records what is on the page. The bank-account recognizer was removed in September 2026, so no type covers this.

Malformed: RBI requires four ALPHABETIC characters at positions 1-4 and this has an '8' at position 3 (verified at 8x). IN_IFSC therefore cannot fire, by specification. A miss here is the image's fault, not the recognizer's — do not 'fix' IN_IFSC to catch it.

A bare 10-digit number in a transaction line, shaped exactly like an Indian mobile number. Genuinely ambiguous: it is a UPI reference, but covering it is the over-redaction this project prefers. Worth a human decision.

h03_bank_account_statement.png.notes: NorthRiver Bank account statement, photographed look, 471x363.

h04_patient_intake_form.png.notes: WellCare Clinic intake form, values HANDWRITTEN in blue ink on a printed form — the hardest OCR case in the corpus. Diabetes and Hypertension are ticked checkboxes with printed labels, so the 'value' is the tick, not the word; a legibility verdict on the printed label is therefore weak evidence. Metformin is the --medical-ner and --protect-clinical case.

pii.note: No published spec; a labels.py case, not a pattern one.

h05_electricity_bill.png.notes: GreenPower Utilities bill. The only non-Bengaluru address in the corpus (Chennai), which is worth keeping if the set is ever trimmed.

h06_library_membership_form.png.notes: Library membership application, ENTIRELY handwritten including the field labels — so labels.py has no printed label geometry to anchor to here. The one page in the corpus that tests the label-anchored path by its absence.

pii.note: No published spec; a labels.py case.

h07_employee_onboarding_form.png.notes: BrightMinds Technologies onboarding form with a headshot at the right. Mixed printed and handwritten values on the same page. Date of Joining and Role are not personal identifiers and are not annotated.

pii.note: The generator renders '5th' with a glyph that reads as 'Sth'. Expect OCR to return either; both are correct against this page.
Presented as a UPI VPA but shaped as an email address, so EMAIL_ADDRESS is the type that should fire, not IN_UPI_VPA.

h08_retail_invoice.png.notes: UrbanKart invoice with a QR code top-right. The QR is the detect()-not-detectAndDecode() case: it must be located and covered whether or not it decodes.

pii.note: The medical-registration recognizer was one of seven removed in September 2026 for having no cited specification. A bare six-digit number with a label beside it: a labels.py case by construction.

h09_doctor_prescription.png.notes: CityCare Hospital prescription, drug lines HANDWRITTEN. Age (34) and Gender are quasi-identifiers and are not annotated, matching documents/. The three medications are the --protect-clinical withdrawal case: a clinician downstream must still be able to read them.

pii.note: Printed beneath the barcode AND encoded in it. Covering the barcode does not cover the printed value; both are needed.

h10_shipping_label.png.notes: SwiftShip label on crumpled paper — heavy creasing and shadow across the text, the most degraded capture in the corpus. Two separate people on one page, which is the case a single-subject assumption gets wrong.

pii.note: DOB 2010 makes this subject a minor.

h11_student_registration_form.png.notes: EduFuture student registration form with a QR code. The parent's signature is an illegible squiggle carrying no readable text, so it is not annotated as a PII item; it still ought to be covered.

pii.note: No published spec; a labels.py case.

pii.text: 12 Green Park Avenue, Indiranagar, Bengaluru - 560038, Karnataka, India

h12_citizen_id_card.png.notes: Same person as h02_community_services_id_card.png — same name, DOB and address on two different document types. Cross-document linkage is a real re-identification route and nothing here measures it.

pii.note: The PNR recognizer was one of seven removed in September 2026 for encoding an invented shape. A six-character alphanumeric beside a PNR label: a labels.py case by construction.

h13_boarding_pass.png.notes: Airline boarding pass. The code block is a dense 2-D symbology printed between 1-D guard bars; annotated as barcode, which is the closest of the three kinds this schema carries.

pii.note: Haemoglobin, below the 12.0-15.0 reference range printed beside it.
Vitamin D, flagged L on the page against a 30-100 range.

h14_lab_report.png.notes: Only the two out-of-range results are annotated, not all six: an in-range value is a weaker health disclosure and a legibility verdict on '96 mg/dL' would be hard to read as a privacy failure. A person may well disagree and annotate all six.

h15_water_bill.png.notes: The QR is labelled 'Scan to pay', so it plausibly encodes the account.

pii.note: Born 2013 — a minor.

h16_school_admission_letter.png.notes: Handwritten PROSE on ruled paper, not a form. Every value sits inside a sentence with no label beside it, so labels.py has nothing to anchor to and the whole page rests on NER over handwriting. The hardest page in the corpus for that reason.

pii.note: A room number with a dated stay is a weak identifier on its own and a strong one beside the guest name. Annotated; a person may disagree.
Already masked to the last four on the page. Whether a masked PAN still needs covering is a policy call, not a detection one.

h18_doctor_prescription.png.notes: Handwritten drug lines. Vitamin D3 60,000 IU is the exact item documents/17 annotates as the --protect-clinical boundary case.

pii.note: Printed under the barcode AND encoded in it; covering one does not cover the other.

h19_shipping_label.png.notes: The only page in the corpus carrying BOTH a barcode and a QR code, and the recipient is the same Sneha Kulkarni as h10_shipping_label.png.

pii.note: Matches the published PAN shape exactly (5 letters, 4 digits, 1 letter), so IN_PAN should fire. Handwritten, which is the test.
Verhoeff checksum FAILS (verified). Third canary for the OCR-tolerant fallback, and the first one that is HANDWRITTEN.

h20_loan_application.png.notes: The densest identifier page in the corpus: PAN and Aadhaar together, both handwritten. Kochi is the only Kerala address here.

pii.note: A bare 10-digit mobile printed as the UPI handle.

h21_cafe_receipt.png.notes: Coffee-shop bill, coffee-stained and creased. Bill number, table and line items are not personal and are not annotated.
